original_question: Is every n-vertex graph representable by an obstacle representation that uses only O(n) polygonal obstacles, where vertices are points in the plane and two vertices are adjacent exactly when the segment joining the corresponding points avoids every obstacle?
target_in_paper: Section 2.5, Open Problem 8: "Is the obstacle number of a graph with n vertices bounded above by a linear function of n?"
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper's intended question. It correctly targets arbitrary n-vertex graphs, uses the plane model with vertices represented by points, uses polygonal obstacles, and asks for a linear upper bound on the number of obstacles needed so that two vertices are adjacent exactly when the joining segment avoids all obstacles.
missing_details: The paper formulates the question in terms of the obstacle number of a graph, meaning the minimum number of obstacles over all obstacle representations of the graph.
The obstacles are specified to be simple polygons.
The quantifier behind the linear bound should be made explicit: one asks whether there exists an absolute constant c such that every n-vertex graph G has obstacle number at most c n.

The nearby definition says each graph vertex is represented by a point in the plane, and uv is an edge if and only if the straight-line segment between the corresponding points does not intersect any obstacle.
The paper includes a standing general-position assumption: the segment joining any two represented vertices does not pass through another represented point or any obstacle vertex.
The question concerns arbitrary graphs; it does not impose extra restrictions such as planarity of the graph or convexity of the obstacles.
refined_question: Let obs(G) denote the obstacle number of a graph G, i.e., the minimum number of simple polygonal obstacles in an obstacle representation of G in which the vertices of G are represented by points in the plane, all represented points and obstacle vertices are in general position, and two vertices u,v are adjacent if and only if the straight-line segment joining their corresponding points avoids every obstacle. Is there an absolute constant c such that every n-vertex graph G satisfies obs(G) <= c n?
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, does every graph on n vertices admit an obstacle representation with at most c n simple polygonal obstacles for some universal constant c?
justification: The draft is aiming at the exact open problem stated in Section 2.5 under Open Problem 8, not at the neighboring lower-bound question (Open Problem 9) or the planar-graph question (Open Problem 11). The surrounding context in Section 2.5 defines obstacle representations, specifies that the obstacles are simple polygons, defines the obstacle number as a minimum over all such representations, and states the general-position assumption. The sentence immediately preceding Open Problem 8 also notes the trivial quadratic upper bound, which confirms that the intended sharpening is specifically a linear upper bound. So the draft is substantively correct, but it should be made fully stand-alone by explicitly naming obs(G), quantifying the O(n) bound as a universal constant times n, and including the paper's representation assumptions.
